meta.purpose: Questions that must be answered before any route or cost decision can reasonably be made. Each answer changes which rows of the cost table are even available.
meta.rule: Where an answer depends on private facts, nothing is assumed. The 'we do not know' column stays unknown until the holder obtains it in writing.

questions.question: What is the lawful origin of the RMB balance?
questions.why: Origin selects the entire route: salary/labour income (current account), property sale, inheritance, pre-emigration assets (capital account), or business proceeds.
questions.we_know: PRC rules split current-account and capital-account money and require a genuine, lawful transaction basis (C01, C02).
how: Obtain the bank statement history and the original credit advices.
Match each credit to its underlying contract, payroll record, sale contract or estate document.
Classify each tranche as current account or capital account before choosing a route.

questions.question: Was PRC individual income tax withheld and paid on that income, and is there a tax certificate?
questions.why: For a foreign individual, the conversion requires source-of-funds materials including tax documents (C06). Unpaid PRC tax is the layer that actually costs 3%-45% or a flat 20%.
questions.we_know: The rule requires tax documents; the IIT rates are 3%-45% / 5%-35% / 20% (C06, C14).
questions.we_do_not_know: Whether tax was withheld, whether certificates exist, and whether any period remains unfiled.
how: Request the individual income tax payment records from the competent tax authority.
Ask the former employer for withholding certificates.
If nothing was withheld, obtain advice on the filing position before approaching the bank.

questions.question: How does SAFE classify the holder: domestic individual (境内个人) or foreign individual (境外个人), and is there a Foreign Permanent Resident ID?
questions.why: The USD 50,000 annual purchase quota applies to domestic individuals and only to foreign individuals holding a PR ID (C04, C07).
questions.we_know: The quota wording and the PR-ID condition (C04, C07).
questions.we_do_not_know: The holder's SAFE category and PR-ID status.
how: Check residence days and domicile against the definition in the FX regulations.
Ask the bank, in writing, which category it will book the account under.
If a PR ID exists, confirm it is accepted for quota purposes at that branch.

questions.question: When was each CNY tranche acquired, and what is its USD basis?
questions.why: US tax on any exchange gain depends on the acquisition-date rate against the conversion-date rate, and the USD 200 personal-transaction threshold (C18).
questions.we_know: Section 988(e) excludes personal transactions and only excludes gain of USD 200 or less; translation is at the applicable spot rate (C17, C18).
questions.we_do_not_know: Acquisition dates and rates, and therefore the size of any gain.
how: Build a tranche table: date, CNY amount, spot or consistently posted rate that day, USD basis.
Keep the source for each rate used.
Do not assume a gain is zero because the money 'just sat there'.

questions.question: What is the US reporting history for this account?
questions.why: An account above USD 10,000 aggregate is already an FBAR item, and Form 8938 thresholds can be crossed while the money is still in China (C20).
questions.we_know: FBAR threshold and 8938 thresholds and penalties (C20, C21).
questions.we_do_not_know: Whether prior FBAR/8938 filings exist, and whether any foreign gift or trust reporting applies.
how: Check filed returns for FinCEN 114 and Form 8938 for each year the account existed.
If anything is missing, consider the IRS compliance procedures before moving money.
Keep a written chronology.

questions.question: What is the bank's executable all-in quote today, itemised?
questions.why: The spread is the dominant cost at large amounts and it is not published; only an executable quote settles it (F12).
questions.we_know: The published tariff items that can be read (C23) and a dated published board benchmark (C25).
questions.we_do_not_know: The applied rate, the spread, and any correspondent or receiving-bank deduction for this account.
how: Ask for a written quote stating the applied CNY/USD rate, commission, cable, intermediary and receiving charges.
Compare the quoted rate with the published board on the same timestamp.
Ask what the beneficiary will actually receive in USD.

questions.question: If the money is capital-account money, are the title, tax-clearance and approval documents in hand?
questions.why: Property, inheritance and pre-emigration transfers follow a separate rulebook with approval before conversion (C02, C11).
questions.we_know: Such transfers are governed by separate provisional rules (C11).
questions.we_do_not_know: The local document list, the approval status, and whether the specific rulebook applies.
how: Request the SAFE local-branch document list in writing.
Assemble title documents, tax clearance and identity documents.
Obtain approval before instructing conversion.

questions.question: Is the holder physically in China, or abroad and needing a proxy?
questions.why: The remittance formality may be entrusted to another person with authorisation and the full document set (C09).
questions.we_know: Proxy is expressly permitted for beyond-quota and foreign-individual purchases (C09).
questions.we_do_not_know: The branch's practice on notarised authorisations and whether it will accept a company finance officer as agent.
how: Ask the branch for its authorisation template and notarisation requirement.
Prepare the authorisation, both IDs and the full document set.
Confirm in writing that the agent can sign the conversion and wire.

questions.question: Is the goal liquid USD in a US bank, or spending capacity?
questions.why: Spending capacity has different ceilings (card/POS, ATM RMB 100,000 a year) from a lump-sum conversion (C12).
questions.we_know: The ATM ceiling and the daily card ceiling (C12).
how: Quantify how much must be liquid versus spent over time.
If liquidity is required, only the document or capital-account routes can deliver it at scale.

questions.question: Which bank holds the money, and what is its published tariff?
questions.why: Fees, spreads and acceptance practice are bank-specific; only one bank's tariff was read here (C23, F03).
questions.we_know: One bank's published outward-remittance tariff (C23) and one published rate board (C25).
questions.we_do_not_know: The holding bank's tariff and spread.
how: Obtain the holding bank's current tariff PDF and its rate board.
Compare the two with the numbers here before relying on any fee figure.

questions.question: Has any 'fast' solution been offered - pooling relatives' quotas, a crypto/USDT bridge, or an underground swap?
questions.why: Each of those is separately prohibited, with penalties of up to 30% or more of the amount (C16, C26).
questions.we_do_not_know: What has been proposed to the holder.
how: Write down the proposal and refuse it.
Record who proposed it; if money has already moved, get advice before any further step.

questions.question: What is the plan for the US side after the money arrives?
questions.why: A credit is only usable if the PRC tax was paid and documented, and FEIE-excluded income cannot also generate a credit (C19).
questions.we_know: Form 1116 mechanics, the one-year-back/ten-year-forward carry, and the FEIE/credit conflict (C19).
questions.we_do_not_know: Whether the holder uses FEIE, and whether any PRC tax will be creditable at the treaty rate.
how: Decide FEIE versus credit before the year closes.
Keep PRC tax certificates and the conversion rate evidence.
Report the account on FBAR/8938 as applicable.
